analyzed_vuln.description: Use-after-free in XInclude replacement cleanup: xmlXIncludeIncludeNode() iterates over children of the original <xi:include> node and frees each child with xmlFreeNode(child), but continues traversal using next = child->next taken from nodes that can already be freed indirectly (e.g., malformed/nested fallback/include structures). This leads to a stale sibling pointer and later double-processing/free of nodes, surfacing as UAF in xmlFreeNodeList() (tree.c:3704). Root cause is unsafe mutation/free traversal logic in xmlXIncludeIncludeNode, not xmlFreeNodeList itself.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Triggered via xml harness calling xmlXIncludeProcessFlags() on attacker-controlled XML containing xi:include/xi:fallback nesting. During xmlXIncludeDoProcess phase 2, xmlXIncludeLoadFallback copies fallback children into incTab[nr]->inc. In phase 3, xmlXIncludeIncludeNode() marks include node as XML_XINCLUDE_START and removes fallback children; crafted malformed nested include/fallback layout causes child/sibling links to become invalid during in-place unlink+free traversal, then later list cleanup/replacement touches freed node memory, producing heap-use-after-free in xmlFreeNodeList.
